title: Mango Sticky Rice with Coconut Sauce and Toasted Mung Beans
summary: Steamed glutinous rice soaked in sweetened coconut milk, served with ripe mango, a salty-sweet coconut sauce and crunchy toasted mung beans.
equipment: wok or wide pan with a steamer basket and lid

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
coconut milk (rest of a 400 ml tin)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice in several changes of water until it runs clear. Cover with plenty of cold water and soak for at least 1 h, or overnight in the fridge.

steps.title: Toast the mung beans
steps.text: Cover the mung beans with just-boiled water and leave for 10 min. Drain, spread on kitchen paper to dry for 5 min, then toast in the dry frying pan over medium-high heat for 5-7 min, stirring, until golden and crunchy. Leave to cool.

steps.title: Steam the rice
steps.text: Drain the rice, wrap it loosely in the damp tea towel and set it in the steamer basket. Cover and steam over simmering water for 20-25 min until the grains are translucent and chewy all the way through.

steps.title: Sweeten the coconut milk
steps.text: While the rice steams, warm the 240 ml coconut milk with the sugar and 0.25 tsp salt, stirring until dissolved. Keep warm, but do not let it boil.

steps.title: Soak the rice in coconut
steps.text: Turn the hot rice into a bowl, pour over the sweet coconut milk and stir gently to coat. Cover and leave for 15 min, until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is glossy.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Bring the remaining coconut milk and 0.125 tsp salt to a simmer in the small pan. Stir in the cornflour mixed with 1 tsp water and cook for 1-2 min, stirring, until lightly thickened.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Peel the mangoes, slice off the cheeks and cut them crosswise into 1 cm slices. Fan half a mango beside a mound of rice on each plate, spoon the sauce over the rice and sprinkle with the mung beans.

tips: Use Thai glutinous rice; ordinary rice will not turn sticky.
The ripest, most fragrant mangoes make the dish; Thai or Pakistani varieties are ideal.
Serve the rice warm or at room temperature, never chilled.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftover rice covered at room temperature for up to 4 h, or chill and re-steam for 5 min until soft. Mung beans keep in an airtight jar for a week.
